summary: Component catalog is the generated inventory of exported Bunzai UI entries. scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts scans React components throughout src/ui plus exported create/build/swatch/inject helpers under src/ui/_shared. Authors do not hand-edit the markdown: regenerate it with bun run scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts, and the pre-commit --check gate fails when live exports drift. Each row records Name, source File, TypeScript Signature, optional Doc blurb, and Styles class list. Before building a control, scan this catalog and reuse an existing entry rather than inventing a twin. The two tables distinguish React `.tsx` components from shared `.ts` UI helpers; that distinction is file shape and API role, not a claim that helpers are legacy or awaiting migration. Use the catalog as lookup authority for props and file homes; behavior and layout truth remain in reference/ui and the owning source. Recent entries include the Extension manager, bounded renderer, settings editor, effect-review panel and command menus used by Library and Workbench. ScenePage exposes navigation-ticket and load identifiers for verified host navigation handoff. The catalog also includes the cover composer, context-menu button, reusable proscenium and capped LightRays effect used by the approved premiere layout. It also lists the Context wing, Messenger shell and panels, Booth Chat Summary, shared RoomHeader and Panel, Promptbook editors, Agent and Skill editors, shared Skill conditions and the model picker.

sections.title: Use this for
sections.summary: A short table answers the common UI needs before anyone searches the full catalog. Any action with text uses the Button from the button family, with one primary per view, danger for destructive actions and quiet for low emphasis. An icon-only action is an IconButton with a label; a few options are a Segmented; sections of a room or editor are Tabs; a small on/off filter or tag is a Chip; a clickable row is a ListRow, a menu entry a MenuItem, a fold a Disclosure, a small square target a Tile, a larger face a Card, a tiny mark a Dot. It also names the icon door Ic, SwatchRow and PaintPicker for colors, Toggle for switches, InkDialog or DialogCore for dialogs, and the three theme font tokens. For buttons, color pickers and fonts, lint and the style guard block the alternatives; the rest is the house answer that review checks.

sections.title: Components (React, `.tsx`)
sections.summary: The React table lists exported UI components by name, source file, TypeScript signature and optional documentation and styles links. It covers the shell, Dock, shared controls, Library, Workbench editors, Scenes, Settings, and documentation surfaces. Recent extension entries include the manager, bounded renderer, settings editor, effect-review panel and host command menus. ScenePage exposes navigation-ticket and load identifiers for verified navigation handoff. BookCover composes lorebook presentation, Proscenium frames scene artwork, and LightRays supplies capped premiere beams. Rows are generated discovery metadata, not proof of behavior or a second registry; consult reference/ui and source for the live contract. It also lists Stage AccentRow, Compendium Settings, Participants, Storyboards, the Props wing, Messenger and shared virtualized lists. RoomHeader, Panel, IconPicker, NumberInput, Promptbook views, Agent and Skill editors, shared conditions and model selection also appear.
topics: extension effect review and host command menus

sections.title: Shared UI helpers (`src/ui/_shared`, `.ts`)
sections.summary: Secondary table for exported TypeScript UI helpers under src/ui/_shared whose names begin create, build, swatch, or inject. These are ordinary `.ts` functions rather than JSX components; the table makes no deprecation or migration claim. It uses the same Name, File, Signature, Doc, and Styles columns as the React table. Current entries are buildTimeline from version-history, a pure helper the Updates surface uses to derive release relations and behind counts, and createArtCache, the bounded in-memory art cache that dedupes decrypted portraits and revokes its object URLs on eviction or clear (the app's singleton is also cleared on library lock). Regenerating the catalog adds or removes rows as matching exports change. Open this table when a UI task needs shared computation or construction logic, and open the React table when it needs a rendered control.
